source: Lecture: Sleep plays an active role in memory. During deep sleep, the brain replays experiences from the day, and connections between nerve cells that were used for learning are strengthened. Experiments show that students who sleep after studying recall more the next day than students who stay awake for the same period. Interestingly, sleep does not strengthen everything equally; it seems to favour information that people expect to need in the future. prompt: Describe a place you visited that you would like to visit again. You should say: where it is, when you went there, what you did there, and explain why you would like to visit it again.
text: The place I'd love to go back to is Bandipur, a small hilltop town roughly halfway between Kathmandu and Pokhara. I went there about two years ago, during the Dashain holidays, mainly because a friend had been raving about it and I was curious to see whether it lived up to the hype. And honestly, it did. What struck me first was how quiet it was, because vehicles aren't allowed in the main bazaar, so you can wander along the old stone-paved street without dodging traffic. The buildings are traditional Newari houses with carved wooden windows, and many of them have been turned into little cafes and guesthouses without losing their character. I spent most of my time just walking, I hiked up to a viewpoint called Thani Mai early one morning and watched the clouds lift off the Himalayas, which was genuinely breathtaking. I also visited a huge limestone cave just outside the town. As for why I'd go back, I think it's partly because I only stayed two nights, and I left with the feeling that I'd barely scratched the surface. But more than that, it was the pace of life there. It's one of the few places where I felt completely unhurried, and in a city like Kathmandu that's a rare luxury, so I'd like to go back and stay a little longer next time.

Also too many tourists can damage the environment, like in some trekking routes there is a lot of plastic waste now. And the prices of things become higher, so it is difficult for local people. So I think tourism is good only if it is managed properly and the government makes sure local communities get the benefit.

text: The three speakers discussed whether university lectures should be moved online. The first student argued that recordings give flexibility, so students can study at their own pace and those with part-time jobs don't miss content. The lecturer disagreed, pointing out that attendance falls when lectures are recorded, that students who stop attending get lower marks, and that live teaching lets him notice confusion. The second student suggested a compromise: keep seminars and labs in person, record the large lectures, and add compulsory weekly quizzes. The lecturer accepted this if the quizzes count towards the final grade, and the first student agreed as long as working students are not disadvantaged.
